biography.plain_text: Benigno Toda was a Filipino businessman who acquired control of Philippine Airlines and served as its chairman and president. The carrier returned to government ownership in 1977. His other interests included Cibeles Insurance Corporation, which he owned almost entirely before selling his shares in 1990, and property in the Philippines.
biography.html: Benigno Toda was a Filipino businessman who acquired control of Philippine Airlines and served as its chairman and president. The carrier returned to government ownership in 1977. His other interests included Cibeles Insurance Corporation, which he owned almost entirely before selling his shares in 1990, and property in the Philippines.

confidence.reason: Direct historical statements and first-party accounts support the claims, bounded by the target identity inference.

long_biography.plain_text:
Filipino airline businessman Benigno Toda saw speed as a competitive necessity. In 1970, he argued that carriers would have to embrace supersonic aircraft much as they had adopted jets. During his leadership, Philippine Airlines studied using Concordes on its San Francisco route. The airline ultimately declined to buy them because the aircraft lacked the range for a nonstop Manila-Honolulu flight and carried relatively few passengers.

Toda also commissioned the American designer Cliff May to plan a house in the Philippines. Their contract required May to visit the country twice to complete the project.
